text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hassan meets water and forest engineers to brief them on measures to be taken to curb deforestation.
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali tells Rome FAO food summit that in four decades Morocco had been able to ensure enough food available for its population.
- Prime Minister Filali confers with U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on latest developments on the Western Sahara issue.
- Morocco to extend rest period for fishing stock recovery to four months from two starting 1997.
- Moroccan official say European Union aid to the northern regions is below needs.
- Association of Moroccan cephalopods hails decision to extend fish resting period to four months.
- By acquiring 50 percent of Belgium company Prayon, Office Cherifien des Petroles shows determination to position itself in world markets.
- Figures show that foreign investors prefer to buy existing firms rather than create new ones. Investments in Morocco are expected to total $750 million this year from $450 million last year.
